sec: Bone cells: osteoblasts, osteocytes and osteoclasts · p866

items.exp: Osteoblasts are of mesenchymal origin. (Book p866)

items.q: Match bone formation route — 1) Mesenchymal → chondroblast  2) Mesenchymal → osteoblast via RUNX2 … A) Intramembranous (skull bones, clavicle)  B) Endochondral bone formation
items.exp: Chondroblasts → endochondral; RUNX2-driven osteoblasts → intramembranous (skull, clavicle). (Book p866)

items.q: The transcription factor driving osteoblast differentiation (intramembranous) is:
items.exp: RUNX2 (transcription factor); its defect causes cleido-cranial dysplasia. (Book p866)

items.q: The osteocyte is described as the:
opts: Master regulator of bone formation and resorption
items.exp: Osteocyte = master regulator of bone formation & resorption; mechanoreceptor for loading/unloading and estrogen. (Book p866)
Estrogen kills osteoclasts → ↓ osteoclast numbers (at the level of the joint). (Book p866)

items.q: Unloading forces or estrogen deficiency make osteocytes secrete:
items.exp: Osteocytes produce sclerostin under unloading/estrogen deficiency. (Book p866)

items.q: Match sclerostin actions — 1) Inhibits WNT1  2) Activates osteoclast … A) ↑ bone resorption  B) Inhibits osteoblast differentiation from mesenchymal stem cells
items.exp: Sclerostin inhibits WNT1 (osteoblast formation/action) → blocks osteoblast differentiation, and activates osteoclasts. (Book p866)

items.q: FGF23 produced by osteocytes is the most potent:
items.exp: FGF23 inhibits phosphorus reabsorption at PCT → phosphaturic (most potent). (Book p866)

items.q: Osteoclasts are of ___ origin and use ___ to generate protons for resorption.
items.exp: Osteoclasts: macrophage origin; carbonic anhydrase type 2 generates protons → bone resorption with irregular Howship lacunae. (Book p866)

items.q: The irregular resorption pits made by osteoclasts are called ___.
items.exp: Irregular activity produces Howship lacunae. (Book p866)
